name: Push
description: Movements in which force is applied away from the body's midline, typically extending the elbow and/or shoulder joint against resistance.

subtypes.name: Horizontal Push
subtypes.description: Pushing force applied horizontally, parallel to the ground. Primarily trains the pectoral muscles, anterior deltoid, and triceps.

subtypes.name: Vertical Push
subtypes.description: Pushing force applied vertically overhead. Primarily trains the deltoids, triceps, and upper trapezius.

name: Pull
description: Movements in which force is applied toward the body's midline, typically flexing the elbow and/or retracting the shoulder joint against resistance.

subtypes.name: Horizontal Pull
subtypes.description: Pulling force applied horizontally, parallel to the ground. Primarily trains the rhomboids, middle trapezius, rear deltoids, and biceps.

subtypes.name: Vertical Pull
subtypes.description: Pulling force applied vertically downward. Primarily trains the latissimus dorsi, biceps, and rear deltoid.

name: Hinge
description: A hip-dominant movement in which the hips move posteriorly while the spine maintains a neutral position. The primary muscles are the hamstrings and glutes. Spinal flexion is minimized.

subtypes.name: Bilateral Hip Hinge
subtypes.description: Both feet remain on the ground with equal loading.

subtypes.name: Unilateral Hip Hinge
subtypes.description: Single-leg variation that adds balance and unilateral loading demands.

name: Squat
description: A lower-body movement in which the hips and knees bend simultaneously to lower the body, then return to the starting position. Knee-dominant in nature compared to the hip-dominant hinge.

subtypes.name: Bilateral Squat
subtypes.description: Both feet on the ground with equal loading.

subtypes.name: Unilateral Squat
subtypes.description: Single-leg squat variations. See also: lunge.

name: Lunge
description: A unilateral lower-body movement in which one foot is placed forward (or backward, or to the side) and the rear knee descends toward the floor. Trains the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings with a split-stance base.

subtypes.name: Reverse Lunge
subtypes.description: The rear foot steps backward. Generally considered safer for the knee than the forward lunge.

subtypes.name: Lateral Lunge
subtypes.description: The foot steps to the side, loading the adductors and inner thigh.

name: Carry
description: Movements in which a load is held and transported through space. Challenges grip strength, core stability, and postural endurance. Among the most functional movement patterns.

subtypes.name: Bilateral Carry (Farmer's Walk)
subtypes.description: A load is carried in both hands while walking.

subtypes.name: Unilateral Carry (Suitcase Carry)
subtypes.description: A load is carried in one hand, challenging lateral core stability.

subtypes.name: Overhead Carry (Waiter's Walk)
subtypes.description: A load is carried overhead, training shoulder stability and thoracic extension.

name: Rotation
description: Movements involving rotation of the trunk around the spine's vertical axis. Trains the obliques, transverse abdominis, and hip rotators. Essential for throwing, swinging, and rotational athletic movements.

name: Anti-Rotation
description: Isometric or slow movements in which the core resists a rotational force rather than producing rotation. Trains core stability and spinal protection. Often overlooked but important for injury resilience.

name: Gait
description: Locomotion-based movements including walking, running, skipping, and bounding. Trains the entire lower body and core in a coordinated, alternating pattern.

name: Overhead
description: Movements that involve raising or controlling a load with the arms elevated overhead. Places unique demands on shoulder mobility, rotator cuff stability, and thoracic extension.

name: Bridge / Hip Thrust
description: Supine movements in which the hips are extended upward against gravity from a lying or semi-reclined position. Primarily trains the glutes and hamstrings with the spine largely removed from load-bearing.

subtypes.name: Glute Bridge
subtypes.description: Performed with both feet on the floor and shoulders on the ground.

subtypes.name: Hip Thrust
subtypes.description: Performed with the shoulders elevated on a bench, allowing a greater range of hip extension.

name: Plank / Isometric Core
description: Exercises in which the body holds a fixed position, resisting the pull of gravity on the spine. Trains the core musculature isometrically for stability rather than movement.

subtypes.name: Anti-Extension Plank
subtypes.description: Resisting spinal extension. The classic prone plank.

subtypes.name: Anti-Lateral Flexion
subtypes.description: Resisting lateral bending of the spine.
